title: Ahi Republic
capsule: The Ahi Republic was an unusual Anatolian polity centred on Ankara, organised not as a dynasty but as a fraternal guild of Muslim craftsmen and merchants—the Akhis—operating under Mongol suzerainty after the Seljuk defeat at the Battle of Köse Dağ in 1243. Founded by the saint and guild master Ahi Evran, the Akhi brotherhood governed Ankara and its surroundings through elected sheikhs holding the title ahibaba, making it more a communal republic of tradespeople than a conventional sultanate. The Arab traveller Ibn Battuta visited Ankara in 1333 and left a vivid description of the Akhis' hospitality and civic organisation. Ottoman ruler Orhan seized Ankara in 1354, and Murad I permanently extinguished Ahi political authority by 1362, absorbing Ankara into the expanding Ottoman state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Ahi polity's existence and character are confirmed by Ibn Battuta's eyewitness account and later Ottoman sources, but its exact territorial jurisdiction beyond Ankara itself is poorly defined in surviving records.
